Finding 2: Session Connect and Disconnect
Impact is 1.55 active sessions, 16.02% of total activity.
---------------------------------------------------------
Session connect and disconnect calls were consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is 1.55 active sessions, 16.02% of total activity.
   --------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate application logic for possible reduction of connect and
      disconnect calls. For example, you might use a connection pool scheme in
      the middle tier.


Finding 3: Soft Parse
Impact is 1.04 active sessions, 10.77% of total activity.
---------------------------------------------------------
Soft parsing of SQL statements was consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is 1.04 active sessions, 10.77% of total activity.
   --------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate application logic to keep open the frequently used cursors.
      Note that cursors are closed by both cursor close calls and session
      disconnects.

   Recommendation 2: Database Configuration
   Estimated benefit is 1.04 active sessions, 10.77% of total activity.
   --------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Consider increasing the session cursor cache size by increasing the
      value of parameter "session_cached_cursors".
   Rationale
      The value of parameter "session_cached_cursors" was "1000" during the
      analysis period.


Finding 4: Java Execution
Impact is .96 active sessions, 9.98% of total activity.
-------------------------------------------------------
JAVA execution consumed significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is .96 active sessions, 9.98% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Look at the "Top SQL Statements" finding for SQL statements consuming
      significant time in Java execution. For example, the PL/SQL statement
      with SQL_ID "9khk1b9ht609p" is responsible for 94% of Java execution
      time during the analysis period.


Finding 5: Unusual "Other" Wait Event
Impact is .96 active sessions, 9.94% of total activity.
-------------------------------------------------------
Wait event "OJVM: Generic" in wait class "Other" was consuming significant
database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is .96 active sessions, 9.94% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate the cause for high "OJVM: Generic" waits. Refer to Oracle's
      "Database Reference" for the description of this wait event.
   Action
      Look at the "Top SQL Statements" finding for SQL statements consuming
      significant time on the "OJVM: Generic" wait event. For example, the
      PL/SQL statement with SQL_ID "9khk1b9ht609p" is responsible for 95% of
      these waits.

   Recommendation 2: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is .96 active sessions, 9.94% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate the cause for high "OJVM: Generic" waits in Service
      "SYS$USERS".

   Recommendation 3: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is .79 active sessions, 8.2% of total activity.
   -----------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate the cause for high "OJVM: Generic" waits in Module "JDBC
      Thin Client".

   Recommendation 4: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is .17 active sessions, 1.74% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate the cause for high "OJVM: Generic" waits in Module
      "oracle@kuber-db".

   Symptoms That Led to the Finding:
   ---------------------------------
      Wait class "Other" was consuming significant database time.
      Impact is .99 active sessions, 10.29% of total activity.


Finding 6: Hard Parse Due to Invalidations
Impact is .55 active sessions, 5.69% of total activity.
-------------------------------------------------------
Cursors were getting invalidated due to DDL operations. This resulted in
additional hard parses which were consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is .55 active sessions, 5.69% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate appropriateness of DDL operations.

   Symptoms That Led to the Finding:
   ---------------------------------
      Hard parsing of SQL statements was consuming significant database time.
      Impact is 1.14 active sessions, 11.86% of total activity.


Finding 7: Undersized SGA
Impact is .13 active sessions, 1.32% of total activity.
-------------------------------------------------------
The SGA was inadequately sized, causing additional I/O or hard parses.
The value of parameter "sga_target" was "184320 M" during the analysis period.

   Recommendation 1: Database Configuration
   Estimated benefit is .03 active sessions, .26% of total activity.
   -----------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Increase the size of the SGA by setting the parameter "sga_target" to
      195840 M.

   Symptoms That Led to the Finding:
   ---------------------------------
      Hard parsing of SQL statements was consuming significant database time.
      Impact is 1.14 active sessions, 11.86% of total activity.
